turns.response_html:
To visualize your Pascal class in Cytoscape.js, we need to bridge the gap between your recursive object structure and the flat Elements array (nodes and edges) that Cytoscape requires.

Your current implementation creates a Binary Tree where each node produces two unique children. Even if their values are the same, they are distinct objects in memory.

1. The Strategy

We will add a method to your Pascal class (or a standalone function) that performs a Breadth-First Search (BFS) or Depth-First Search (DFS) through your nodes. We'll assign each XNode a unique ID based on its memory reference to ensure the edges connect correctly.

2. Implementation for JSFiddle

You can copy-paste these three sections into the respective panels in JSFiddle.

HTML

We need a container for the graph and the Cytoscape library.

<script src="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/cytoscape/3.26.0/cytoscape.min.js"></script>
<script src="https://unpkg.com/dagre@0.7.4/dist/dagre.js"></script>
<script src="https://cytoscape.org/cytoscape.js-dagre/cytoscape-dagre.js"></script>

<div id="cy"></div>

CSS

#cy {
  width: 100%;
  height: 100vh;
  display: block;
  background-color: #f9f9f9;
}

JavaScript

Include your classes first, then add the conversion logic and the Cytoscape initializer:

// ... [Your XNode, Triangle, and Pascal classes here] ...

function visualizePascal(pascalInstance) {
  const elements = [];
  const visited = new Set();
  let idCounter = 0;

  // Map to store object references to unique IDs
  const nodeMap = new Map();

  function traverse(node) {
    if (!node || visited.has(node)) return;
    visited.add(node);

    // Assign ID if not exists
    if (!nodeMap.has(node)) {
      nodeMap.set(node, `n${idCounter++}`);
    }

    const currentId = nodeMap.get(node);

    // Add the Node to elements
    elements.push({
      data: { id: currentId, label: node.value.toString() }
    });

    // Handle Left Child
    if (node.left) {
      if (!nodeMap.has(node.left)) nodeMap.set(node.left, `n${idCounter++}`);
      const leftId = nodeMap.get(node.left);
      
      elements.push({ data: { id: `${currentId}-${leftId}`, source: currentId, target: leftId } });
      traverse(node.left);
    }

    // Handle Right Child
    if (node.right) {
      if (!nodeMap.has(node.right)) nodeMap.set(node.right, `n${idCounter++}`);
      const rightId = nodeMap.get(node.right);
      
      elements.push({ data: { id: `${currentId}-${rightId}`, source: currentId, target: rightId } });
      traverse(node.right);
    }
  }

  traverse(pascalInstance.triangle.head);
  return elements;
}

// 1. Initialize your data
const myPascal = new Pascal(3); // Depth of 3

// 2. Initialize Cytoscape
const cy = cytoscape({
  container: document.getElementById('cy'),
  elements: visualizePascal(myPascal),
  style: [
    {
      selector: 'node',
      style: {
        'background-color': '#666',
        'label': 'data(label)',
        'color': '#fff',
        'text-valign': 'center',
        'text-halign': 'center',
        'width': 40,
        'height': 40
      }
    },
    {
      selector: 'edge',
      style: {
        'width': 2,
        'line-color': '#ccc',
        'target-arrow-color': '#ccc',
        'target-arrow-shape': 'triangle',
        'curve-style': 'bezier'
      }
    }
  ],
  layout: {
    name: 'dagre', // Uses the dagre extension for hierarchical layout
    rankDir: 'TB'
  }
});

3. Key Observations & Tips

  • The Dagre Layout: Standard Pascal's Triangles are hierarchical. I included the dagre extension script in the HTML. It makes the "top-down" structure look much cleaner than the default random or grid layouts.
  • Recursive vs. DAG: In a standard Pascal's Triangle, the "left" child of a right-node and the "right" child of a left-node usually merge into the same object (e.g., the 2 in the third row).
    • Your current logic creates two separate nodes for that position.
    • If you decide to modify your code to reuse nodes, the nodeMap in my visualization code will automatically detect that and draw two arrows pointing to the same node (turning the tree into a Directed Acyclic Graph).
  • Depth Caution: Because your current code creates a full binary tree ($2^n$ nodes), setting depth higher than 10 might cause JSFiddle to hang or Cytoscape to lag significantly.
